rules: Precedence: an IMP code wins over an R code, and an R code wins over an X code. A reason naming an external fact that a v0.3.0 change mitigates gets that IMP code.
X-HIST and X-ENV notes cite the IMP or R code that handles any actionable part, when one exists.
X-FALSE covers premises untrue of v0.2.0 as well as causal links that do not hold.
Ongoing constraints of a solo, unfunded project are X-ENV when nothing in the plugin can change them.

IMP-32.title: Remeasured cost
IMP-32.detail: Estimate constants and the README cost table come from the v0.2.0 full run (per-agent totals, 38 output tokens per reason); the basis names the version, model and what the totals count.

IMP-33.title: Version stamps
IMP-33.detail: run.json and the five-whys.json header record plugin_version read from plugin.json; init and status print it; a MEASURED constant labels the estimate and a docs test ties it to the README.

IMP-34.title: Changelog with evidence
IMP-34.detail: CHANGELOG.md holds a dated entry per version with its verification evidence; RELEASING.md points evidence there; a docs test requires an entry for the manifest version.

IMP-35.title: Release gates by change kind
IMP-35.detail: RELEASING.md: prompt, agent, dispatch or estimate changes need a model-invoked run through /five-whys (checkout loaded with --plugin-dir) or the eval; figures name their version; review a ledger sample; check option count.

IMP-36.title: Test the checkout before publishing
IMP-36.detail: README and RELEASING.md document `claude --plugin-dir .` so unpublished SKILL.md and agent text run in a real session before the marketplace entry changes.

IMP-37.title: Invocation parsed in code
IMP-37.detail: A parse subcommand reads the raw $ARGUMENTS on stdin and returns the problem, init flags, --yes, --resume and errors for unknown options, honoring a -- separator; SKILL.md Step 1 uses it.

IMP-38.title: Confirmation decided in code
IMP-38.detail: init returns confirm: true when agents exceed CONFIRM_AGENTS; SKILL.md obeys the flag; a docs test ties the constant to the prose.

IMP-39.title: Settings recorded and shown
IMP-39.detail: run.json stores the options given to init and the plugin version; index.md opens with the shape, model, wave size and version that produced the tree.

IMP-40.title: Per-tier model flags removed
IMP-40.detail: --root-model and --branch-model go: unmeasured, unreachable from /five-whys, and they multiplied configurations. plan still honors tier fields in older run.json files.

IMP-41.title: Options with stated purpose and a count
IMP-41.detail: The README options table says why each option exists; a docs test pins the number of skill options so additions and removals are deliberate.

IMP-42.title: Later waves see finished branches
IMP-42.detail: Branch prompts list the first-level reasons of branch fragments that already validate, beside the root's reasons, so staged waves reduce cross-branch repeats.

IMP-43.title: Smaller default waves
IMP-43.detail: max_parallel defaults to 5 instead of filling the 20-subagent cap, pairing with IMP-42 and lighter machine load; --max-parallel 20 remains for speed.

IMP-44.title: Orchestration replay test
IMP-44.detail: A unit test walks SKILL.md's loop with fake agents: parse, init, plan --record, fragments, check, status, assemble; plus a failing agent reaching stuck and assemble --partial.

IMP-45.title: Stemmed and cross-branch hygiene
IMP-45.detail: Tokens strip common suffixes; pairs in different level-1 branches at 0.45 or more are listed as cross_branch leads; flags carry both texts; filters and cutoffs appear in hygiene.json.

IMP-46.title: Check sees the real ancestors
IMP-46.detail: For a branch fragment inside a run, check loads the root's chain for that node so restatement warnings compare against real ancestors and the root's reasons.

IMP-47.title: Paraphrase pairs from a real tree
IMP-47.detail: tests/fixtures/pairs.json holds labeled convergent and distinct pairs from the v0.2.0 tree; a test records how many the heuristic catches and fails if detection regresses.

IMP-48.title: Read plan sized by bytes
IMP-48.detail: assemble lists Read offsets in index.md from line byte sizes under a budget, replacing the fixed 400-line rule in SKILL.md and README.

IMP-49.title: Agent guidance beyond software problems
IMP-49.detail: why-expander.md gains a non-software example, a rule for problems with nothing to read, leaves that keep a concrete tie to their chain, and assumptions for ungrounded reasons.

IMP-50.title: Thin-problem eval case
IMP-50.detail: A second eval case runs a one-line non-software problem through --smoke --yes; RELEASING.md cites graders/criteria.md instead of paraphrasing it.

IMP-51.title: Auditable ledger tooling
IMP-51.detail: ledger.py rounds: rule fragments with inheritance recorded as via, sample with ancestors and code detail, summary of X notes citing codes; catalog precedence rules.

IMP-52.title: Hygiene in its own module
IMP-52.detail: Similarity code moves to scripts/hygiene.py beside fivewhys.py, keeping one entry point for SKILL.md and agents while the largest self-contained concern gets its own file.

IMP-53.title: Round-2 record
IMP-53.detail: docs/self-improvement holds round 1 and round 2 side by side, with measured facts, a recorded sample audit and a review of the plugin made outside the tree.

R-01.title: Declined: plugin-side ranking, synthesis, pruning or root-cause selection
R-01.detail: Analysis stays with the user. Mechanical leads such as IMP-45 cross-branch pairs are the allowed aid.

R-02.title: Declined: embeddings, third-party packages, API keys or network calls
R-02.detail: Would break the zero-dependency offline install and send problem text off the machine.

R-03.title: Declined: model judge inside the blocking fix loop
R-03.detail: Flaky verdicts loop repair cycles and multiply cost.

R-04.title: Declined: incomplete trees
R-04.detail: Early stopping, variable breadth, not-applicable slots or pruning break the complete-tree requirement.

R-06.title: Out of scope: social or organizational remedies
R-06.detail: Recruiting reviewers or testers, announcements, curated-marketplace submission, paying for review. Not plugin changes.

R-11.title: Declined: token usage relayed through the orchestrator
R-11.detail: Usage reaches only the model's tool results; copying numbers through prose is unreliable. Measure from subagent logs per release instead (IMP-35).

R-12.title: Declined: prompt-length term in the estimate
R-12.detail: Measured prompts are about 1.7k of 63k tokens per branch; generation and evidence reading dominate (IMP-32 remeasures those).

R-13.title: Declined: live evals, secrets or model runs in CI
R-13.detail: Paid on every push, secrets exposed to Bash-capable agents, unavailable to forks, nondeterministic. Evals run locally per RELEASING.md.

R-14.title: Declined: model-based convergence or quality review inside the plugin
R-14.detail: Nondeterministic, costs a second full read and crosses into analysis. IMP-45 lists mechanical cross-branch leads instead.

R-15.title: Declined: cross-links or graph structure in the tree schema
R-15.detail: The deliverable is a complete strict tree; relationships stay in hygiene.json.

R-16.title: Declined: persistent settings files or environment defaults
R-16.detail: Shape and model are per-problem choices; a stale stored default could silently launch a costly run. Flags stay explicit and are recorded (IMP-39).

R-17.title: Declined: telemetry, phoning home or cross-run collection
R-17.detail: Problem statements can be confidential and there is no backend; run.json records settings locally (IMP-39).

R-18.title: Deferred: studies needing many paid runs
R-18.detail: Model-tier quality, same-model variance, multi-domain benchmarks, grader reliability and large labeled corpora. Recorded as known limitations.

R-19.title: Declined: a headless runner owning the dispatch loop
R-19.detail: claude -p subprocesses would spawn separate sessions, lose inline progress and need their own auth; the loop stays with the orchestrating model, helped by IMP-37, IMP-38 and IMP-44.

R-20.title: Declined: developer tooling dependencies in CI
R-20.detail: Linters, coverage and complexity tools add installs to a stdlib project; structure is handled by IMP-52 and review.

R-21.title: Declined: fragment provenance markers
R-21.detail: Any session can write identical bytes, so a marker proves nothing; authorship is checked in transcripts by the eval grader.

R-22.title: Declined: fault injection or tunable attempt limits for rehearsal
R-22.detail: IMP-44 drives the stuck and partial paths deterministically with fake agents, without new options.

X-DONE.title: Already resolved
X-DONE.detail: The note says what resolved it, usually a fact above or an existing v0.2.0 feature.

X-FALSE.title: Premise untrue or causal link does not hold
X-FALSE.detail: The note names the contradicting fact.

X-ENV.title: Outside the plugin's control
X-ENV.detail: Platform, model, ecosystem or the project's standing circumstances. Cite a mitigating code when one exists.

X-HIST.title: Past motivation or process, nothing further to change
X-HIST.detail: Explains how v0.2.0 came to be. Cite the code that handles any actionable part.
